thread.title: S&P 500, Dow Jones Futures Dive As Investors Lose White House Ally Gary Cohn – Financial News USA

author: Andre T
title: S&P 500, Dow Jones Futures Dive As Investors Lose White House Ally Gary Cohn – Financial News USA
text:
by Andre T · March 7, 2018 
Futures for the S&P 500 index, Dow Jones industrial average and Nasdaq 100 fell sharply early Wednesday morning after President Trump’s chief economic advisor Gary Cohn resigned as Trump remains committed to imposing a 25% tariff on steel and a 10% tariff on aluminum. 
X 
The former Goldman Sachs president, who will leave at an unspecified date, was widely respected on Wall Street and a fierce opponent of protectionist economic policies in the White House. His exit undercuts hopes for Trump to delay or modify those tariffs. It also means Cohn won’t be around to argue against further protectionist moves. 
At a trade policy meeting at the White House Tuesday, Trump sought assurance that everyone would publicly back the tariffs, but Cohn did not answer, Bloomberg reported. Hours later, he was gone. 
Stocks had rallied in the last few days on optimism that the final tariffs would not be as damaging as feared. So Cohn’s abrupt departure suggests that the major averages would come under near-term pressure. 
S&P 500 futures fell 1.3% below fair value. Dow Jones futures tumbled 1.5%, Nasdaq 100 futures sank 1.2%. The dollar also retreated. 
Over in Asia, Japan’s Nikkei lost 0.6% intraday. 
Apple (AAPL) fell 1.6% in late trading. Boeing (BA) lost 2.7% and General Motors (GM) sank 2.6%; both are big steel and aluminum users. United Technologies (UTX), one of the most exposed to the proposed tariffs, was off 2.7%. DowDuPont (DWDP), which said steel tariffs hurt the case for new U.S. plant, slid 2.5%. 
Apple, Boeing, DowDuPont and United Technologies are all Dow Jones components. 
U.S. Steel (X) climbed 2.7%.
